headline: Red Sox pitching implodes early in another frustrating loss to Seattle
morning_brew: I watched that absolute disaster last night and I am still scrubbing my eyes with a rag just to process what the hell I saw. Giving up eight runs to Seattle before the fourth inning is the kind of stuff that would make my cousin Jimmy look like a Cy Young candidate on the mound. Paez didn't have it, the defense looked like they were allergic to the baseball, and suddenly we are staring at another hole we couldn't climb out of if we had a ladder and an extra three hours. It is the same horror movie with a different low-budget remake, and frankly, I am getting exhausted from paying good money to watch us serve up batting practice.

The bats tried to make a game of it late, and I will give them credit for not packing up their bags and heading to the airport when things got ugly, but that early deficit was a mountain they just couldn't scale. You cannot ask a bullpen to save your skin every single night after the starter leaves you in the weeds before the sun even finishes setting over the Fens. I am officially pulling a small withdrawal from the Duck Boat fund until further notice, because watching this team play from behind is taking years off my life, but here I am, waiting for the rubber match today.

We have another date with the Mariners this afternoon before we pack our bags for Baltimore. If we do not start getting some actual command out of the rotation, all this strength of schedule talk is going to be moot by the time we hit the middle of September. Linda from Lynn is right about one thing: I will believe this team is ready for October when I see them actually show up for a full nine innings without giving me a migraine. Let's hope for a hell of a lot better showing today.

news_digest.headline: 2026 MLB playoff contenders: Remaining strength of schedule
news_digest.dans_take: The path to the postseason is right there, but it will not matter if we keep handing out wins like candy.

news_digest.headline: TreVeyon Henderson battling ankle injury ahead of opener
news_digest.dans_take: Tough news to wake up to, let's hope it is just a minor bump and he is good to go for the season opener.

trend_watch.trend: Gave up 8 earned runs in 3.2 innings
trend_watch.dans_take: Pops always said if a pitcher cannot get through five, he is basically just a glorified batting practice machine. He would have had plenty of words for this mess.
At least someone in the lineup remembers how to find the barrel of the bat. He was the only guy who didn't look like he was swinging a garden rake.
He actually looked like a professional out there, which is a massive relief considering the arson squad usually takes over the second the starter leaves.
